title: Reconcile multipart input echoes and sideband messages in metering pipeline
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Summary: Intermittent out-of-band frames and client-side echoing in multipart websocket sessions are producing duplicated input tokens and sideband metadata messages that are being double-counted by the metering pipeline. This ticket scopes investigating and fixing the reconciliation logic so final per-session billing reflects true user input and model output only.

Background: We recently observed customer reports and dashboard anomalies where small bursty sessions (clients that send rapid multipart frames plus metadata-only sideband messages such as typing indicators, acknowledgement echoes, and file-attachment hints) show inflated input token totals. Root cause hypotheses include: (1) client echo behavior where the gateway re-emits certain frames during reconnects, (2) our prefix-merge logic treating sideband frames as content-bearing, and (3) race conditions in checkpoint finalization for sessions that switch models midstream.

Scope: Fix is limited to the metering pipeline and gateway normalization layers for hosted and dedicated websocket flows (not on-prem agent for this change). Work includes: (a) canonicalizing what constitutes a billable input frame, (b) introducing deterministic de-duplication keys for multipart fragments and sideband messages, (c) backfill/repair tooling for recent affected sessions, and (d) adding end-to-end tests and dashboards to detect regressions.

Out of scope: Changes to client SDKs, billing UI, or pricing model. On-prem/private will get a backported patch later depending on compatibility testing.
acceptance_criteria: Metering pipeline ignores metadata-only sideband frames (typing, ack, presence) when computing input token counts
Duplicate multipart fragments (same client-fragment-id + sequence) are deduplicated deterministically across reconnects
Backfill job produced reconciliation report and repaired token tallies for >99% of identified affected sessions in the last 72 hours
E2E test harness reproduces reconnect + client-echo scenario and asserts no >1% drift in final billed tokens compared to ground truth
New dashboard tile (metering/streaming/echo-dup-rate) shows <0.1% duplicate-frame rate in GA traffic within 24h of rollout
Rollout plan documented and rollback toggle implemented in runtime-2.3.0
risks: Over-eager filtering could drop legitimate content-bearing fragments (attachments or short inline messages) if metadata tagging is inconsistent
Repair/backfill might temporarily change historical billing for a subset of customers (requires legal/product sign-off)
Edge cases remain for encrypted or third-party-proxied websockets that preserve different metadata conventions
implementation_plan: Stage 1: Instrument - add tracing to gateway to tag frame provenance and emit candidate dedupe-key (3d)
Stage 2: Normalize - update gateway + runtime shard to classify frames as content vs metadata (4d)
Stage 3: Pipeline - apply deterministic dedupe and canonicalization in metering joiner; add idempotent finalization semantics (5d)
Stage 4: Backfill - implement repair job with dry-run reporting and manual approval gate (3d)
Stage 5: Test & rollout - e2e tests in staging, canary rollout with dashboard alerts, rollback toggle (2d)
Total (sprint-sized): ~17 engineering days split across two engineers + SRE on-call window
notes: Initial customer impact ticket: CS-5123 (customer reported % discrepancies in small-burst sessions)
SRE consulted on retention windows for intermediate dedupe state (recommended 7 days TTL)
We should coordinate legal/product messaging for any billing adjustments from backfill
